Sources were placed on the floor, at 1 m in a heat-source plume (Table 4 'S2: occupant source') and as a 'momentum' source in the breathing plane (cough-like). Exposure is normalised breathing-plane concentration CN. The highest CN came from the breathing-plane momentum source (up to 45 and 72.6). The occupant-plume source S2 gave breathing-plane CN of 0.04-2.9, not consistently higher than the floor source. Main conclusion: with good mixing, source location matters little; for 7 um particles, source location and local airflow dominate. The paper does not show that near-body sources give far higher exposure per unit mass.
contexts.suggested_fix: Cite Rim 2010 only for 'source location and local airflow govern exposure when mixing is poor', and rest the near-body claim on licina2017 (personal cloud), or add a study that compares body-adjacent and remote sources directly.
